Under Tonga's Constitution, nearly all trade stops on Sunday, running from midnight to midnight by law. But the line has moved across the years: in 2019, church leaders voiced concern over hotels and resorts opening for tourists; in May 2025, the government announced a review, with the Prime Minister stating exemptions are for essential services; and in June 2025, an RNZ report noted that restaurants serving visitors hold exemptions, while Tongans often eat out after church. As of October 2026, no outcome of the Sunday review has been announced. If a country chooses a constitutional day of rest, should it make an exception for restaurants and visitors, or keep the rule absolute for everyone? Say which side you lean toward, and say why. And tell us where you're watching from, and what is on your table tonight. 👇
